Chapter 5: Waiting on God’s Timing and Trusting the Process
Let’s be honest—patience isn’t always easy, especially when it comes to matters of the heart. The longing for connection, for someone to share life with, is just so deeply human, isn’t it? But here’s the thing—when it comes to courtship, waiting isn’t a waste of time or just a period of frustration. It’s actually a season for growth, for trust, and for getting ready.
Waiting on God’s timing is all about recognizing that not every season is meant for romance or marriage. Sometimes the road ahead feels crystal clear. Other times? It’s filled with questions, uncertainty, maybe even a little longing. And in those moments, it’s tempting to rush, to settle, or to try to force things to happen. But here’s something to remember—the wisdom in waiting is all about trusting that God’s plans are good, even when we can’t see the whole picture.
Now, waiting isn’t just sitting back and doing nothing. It’s active. It looks like:
- Growing as a person—using this time of singleness to build your character, deepen your faith, and chase after your goals. - Staying connected with God—praying, seeking guidance, and being honest about your hopes and desires. - Finding contentment—learning how to really enjoy the present moment, instead of always wishing for what’s next. - Being open—sometimes that means letting go of a relationship or a dream that just isn’t the best fit for you.
You know, waiting can sometimes feel like you’re just standing at a crossroads, unsure which way to go. That’s exactly when trust gets real. Surrendering control, embracing patience, and taking one step at a time—this is how we learn to lean on God’s wisdom, not just our own.
Think about it—this season is also a chance to figure out what really matters to you. What qualities do you want in a future spouse? What kind of relationship will truly honor God and bring lasting joy? Taking time to reflect on those questions means you’ll step into future relationships with so much more clarity and confidence.
And just because you’re waiting doesn’t mean shutting yourself off from every opportunity. It means moving forward only when you feel at peace, when things are clear, and when you truly sense God leading you. Sometimes that means saying “no” to something good, just so you can wait for what’s best.
I know, this approach goes against the grain, especially in a world that’s all about instant results and quick fixes. But here’s the truth—the patience you practice now is never wasted. The fruit of waiting? Deeper relationships, stronger faith, and a joy that lasts. When you trust the process, you just might find that the wait was more than worth it.
